purpose: Expand Predators in Power into a current-status, child-safeguarding and legal-posture intelligence layer without converting office, association, rumors or unresolved allegations into guilt.
currentStatusRule: A subject is shown as currently in power only when a separately sourced role record identifies a current, acting, suspended or on-leave position and was checked within the configured freshness window. A role held when charged but later resigned is shown as former, with both dates and sources preserved.
coverageRule: Every editorially approved child-focused conduct record with a separately sourced qualifying power role must appear in the expanded output or cause the build to fail. Manual eligibility flags cannot silently omit a qualifying subject.
claimsReviewRule: Anonymous claims, social-media rumors, guilt by association and unsupported child-offence insinuations about living people are not published as named subjects. A named non-adjudicated claim requires an attributable source, exact claim wording, evidence analysis, documented response or right of reply, counter-evidence, proof needed, editorial approval and legal review. Machine matches remain private.
livingPersonClaimRequirements: source must be attributable and independently accessible
the record must quote or accurately summarize the actual public claim without embellishment
right of reply, denial, dismissal, acquittal and counter-evidence must remain attached
the record must state what is not proven
association, friendship, photographs, meetings, donations or shared events cannot establish child offending
boundary: The expanded page is an evidence-classified accountability index. Conviction, charge, inquiry, civil finding, attributed allegation, analytical hypothesis and rumor are different states. Charges are not convictions. A power role is not wrongdoing. A claim-under-review tab records editorial process, not guilt.
